Subject: MSA + DPA redlines and transfer impact questions

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the productive demo last week. Attached are our redlines to the MSA and the proposed DPA. Our procurement and privacy teams have a couple of focused asks before we can proceed to PO: a clear mapping of controller/processor roles in Appendix A, confirmation of the SCCs model Redwood intends to rely on for EU->US transfers, and a short transfer impact note for countries outside the EEA that MedicaSys processes will touch.

Specific items: 
- Appendix A role map seems to treat MedicaSys as "Controller" and Redwood as "Processor" — please confirm and add sub-processor list.
- Section 6.2 (SCCs) — your redline suggested using the new EU SCCs with Module Two; our legal wants explicit statement whether Redwood will act as a data importer under the standard contractual clauses and, if so, which Annexes will be filled.
- Are there any on-prem or private deployment options that would avoid cross-border transfers for our EU tenants?

We attached an annotated SCCs PDF with inline questions (see MedicaSys_SCCs_annotated.pdf). Can you route this to your legal and privacy folks and let us know where Redwood stands? We are aiming to sign by mid-August if the answers are straightforward.

Attachments: MedicaSys_redline_MSA.docx (redline), MedicaSys_redline_DPA.docx (redline), MedicaSys_SCCs_annotated.pdf

Best,
Sara Nguyen
Head of Procurement, MedicaSys

Subject: RE: MSA + DPA redlines and transfer impact questions

Jasmine — thanks for routing. Quick read and proposed negotiation positions below (high-level; see inline comments in the redlines doc which I uploaded to the shared drive).

1) Roles (Appendix A) — Confirm MedicaSys = Controller, Redwood = Processor. We accept that mapping. Add a sub-processor clause that commits to provide a currently-populated sub-processor list and 30 days' notice for additions. We should offer a customer-visible sub-processor register hosted in the Console rather than an exhaustive list in the DPA.

2) SCCs / Transfer approach — Recommend we accept the EU Commission's 2021 SCCs (Module II is typically for controller->processor; we will be the data importer under the SCCs). We should: 
   - Confirm Redwood will act as data importer and sign the SCCs as importer where required.
   - Provide completed Annex I and Annex II templates for the common case (text generation, embeddings) but avoid product-specific annexes until MedicaSys shares processing details.
   - For transfers from the EU to the US, provide the transfer impact assessment summary as a separate one-page memo (non-binding) referencing supplementary safeguards (contractual, technical).

3) Private deployment option — Product can scope a VPC-only deployment per customer but that is an enterprise add-on. It materially changes hosting and support model and will affect pricing and lead time (4–8 weeks setup). Recommend we offer it as an option in the order form but not as a standard term.

4) Security evidence — They asked for SOC2 and encryption details. We should provide the SOC2 Type II report (redacted) and a short security FAQ. I can coordinate with security to prepare the packet.

5) Timeline and escalation — If they need sign-off by mid-August, we should aim to deliver the SCCs Annex templates and transfer-impact memo within 3 business days and clarify the private-deploy timeline as a separate ticket.

Next steps I recommend: Laura to draft the redline responses and an Annex I/II template, Jasmine to propose option pricing for private deployment, Rachel to capture timeline in HubSpot and set a follow-up.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
